A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same STaR study, authors, tasks and core experiments. The text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: V1 reports original model evaluations on RCC-8 and interval algebra, including accuracy, F1, per-relation results and token-usage analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those original evaluations and adds empirical analyses of path recovery, operation complexity and shortcut use, together with a model reasoning trace.

M1.justification: The evaluated models, integer-encoded inputs, composition-table prompts, training and inference procedures remain unchanged. V2 adds behavioral analysis of algebraic-closure simulation without introducing a new model or inference method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate RCC-8 and interval-algebra tasks from STaR with the same stated training and test coverage. The new diagnostics partition existing instances by graph complexity and shortcut availability.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Table 1, Figures 3-4 and Table 2 are unchanged, including o3-mini and R1-distilled Qwen 7B/14B. The additional diagnostics use these existing reasoning models.

E3.justification: The original evaluation settings, sample counts and token budgets are retained. Section 6.3 and Appendix C.2 introduce diagnostic procedures measuring recovered paths, stratifying accuracy by trivial-path availability, and relating performance to intersection counts and a union-cardinality proxy.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands failure analysis through path-recovery distributions, intersection/union complexity analyses and trivial-path comparisons in Figures 6-7 and 12-13. Appendix D adds a full Qwen-14B reasoning example. V1's classification, token-length and nonresponse analyses remain.

E5.justification: Figure 7 introduces Spearman correlations with p-values and explicitly labeled ±1σ uncertainty reporting. The existing median/IQR token-usage reporting and global sampling seed of 0 remain unchanged; no increased repeated-run count is reported.

E6.justification: The original benchmark plots and Tables 2-4 retain their values. Substantial diagnostic results are added, including low path-recovery fractions, shortcut-stratified accuracy and negative accuracy/intersection correlations: -0.65 for RCC-8 and -0.66 for IA in Figure 7(a).

T1.justification: V2 explicitly defines trivial paths using equality relations and at most one other relation, and states the resulting solution rule, extending v1's all-equality example. The core rule equations, composition tables and Appendix A complexity arguments remain unchanged.

C1.justification: V1 primarily claims limited systematic generalization. V2's title, abstract, introduction and conclusion elevate a specific contribution: LRMs shallowly simulate algebraic closure, struggle with traversal and intersection, and can exploit trivial-path heuristics without task-specific training.

C2.justification: V2 develops an operation-level explanation linking failures to incomplete path enumeration and intersection complexity. It also argues that LRMs exploit shortcuts when they find suitable paths, extending v1's distinction between fine-tuned LLM heuristics and o3-mini's error-prone systematic reasoning. The Limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 documents how the new intersection and union-complexity quantities are calculated and supplies an inspectable reasoning trace in Appendix D. Appendix B retains the hardware, hyperparameters, libraries, token limits and prompt templates.

R1.justification: V2 adds Lin et al. (2025, ZebraLogic) and Saparov et al. (2025) to position the algorithmic and search interpretation. It removes discussion and references concerning STBench, Yamada et al. (2024) and Path-of-thoughts. Most research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are revised, with targeted edits to the introduction, related work, results and conclusion. Analysis gains numbered subsections, Appendix C is subdivided, and Appendix D is added; the overall section order and much existing prose remain.

P2.justification: The visual presentation expands substantially through four new analytical figures and a multipage boxed reasoning transcript. Existing benchmark plots and classification tables are redistributed across pages; earlier appendix diagrams, prompts and the nonresponse figure are retained with renumbering.

improvement.justification: The new diagnostics and Appendix D trace strengthen failure-mode explanations that v1 supported mainly through scores and token lengths. The gain is limited by correlational support for the stronger algorithm-simulation claims and unavailable full o3-mini traces. A new reporting ambiguity also remains: Figure 12's IA caption conflicts with Appendix C.2's RCC-8 description.
